title: UPSERT conflict-target analysis and excluded-row update

scope.rationale: Bounded INSERT now resolves a one-column INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, column UNIQUE, or ordinary UNIQUE-index conflict target and executes one excluded-column assignment against the conflicting row.
excluded_responsibilities: Composite, expression, partial-index, and multiple conflict targets
General assignment expressions or UPSERT WHERE clauses
Full secondary-index maintenance when the conflict-target index itself changes

external_source_responsibilities: Bounded INSERT expression compilation, table mutation batches, foreign-key actions, and ordinary index maintenance
dependencies.caller_closure: The production INSERT compiler and action callback resolve and execute the bounded UPSERT path directly.

inputs: INSERT VALUES with optional one-column ON CONFLICT target
DO NOTHING or DO UPDATE SET column=excluded.column
outputs: Inserted row, unchanged conflicting row, or one updated conflicting row
contracts.ownership: Prepared-statement owner retains target metadata; decoded conflicting records and temporary updated values are released on every result path.
contracts.state_and_results: Unknown or non-unique targets fail preparation. A matching target runs update behavior under the INSERT statement batch and publishes UPDATE hooks and change counts.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Uses the selected database cursor and existing write, transaction-enlistment, update-hook, foreign-key, and index-maintenance paths.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: OOM, malformed records, constraints, and I/O failures roll back the statement batch; a missed target continues as an ordinary insert.

representation_differences: The bounded frontend stores resolved column indexes and a typed collation rather than retaining the C Upsert and Index parse-tree objects.
The native runtime locates an ordinary UNIQUE conflict by a table scan in this bounded path; the canonical secondary index remains the schema-level uniqueness owner.

oracle.protocol: Create the bounded table and UNIQUE index, then compare duplicate IPK update, missed IPK insert, targeted DO NOTHING, ordinary UNIQUE-target update, return codes, row counts, maximum rowid, and payload hash.
internal_observations: prepare, step, and finalize primary codes
resulting table row count, maximum rowid, and payload hash
oracle.normalization: Compare exact C-oracle and native observations after each statement.

assurance.oom: Target schema decoding, prepared metadata, decoded records, and updated payload allocation map OOM to SQLITE_NOMEM and retain statement rollback.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: Uses existing Pager-backed cursor and statement-batch ownership; no new lock protocol.
assurance.malformed_input: Unrecognized targets and assignment shapes fail preparation; corrupt records fail execution.
assurance.continuation: A missed conflict executes the insert, while a failed update rolls back only the current statement batch.
assurance.performance: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY conflicts seek directly. Ordinary one-column UNIQUE targets use a bounded table scan pending broader index-cursor integration.

integration.production_owner: src/core/sql_frontend.zig bounded INSERT compiler and runtime action
integration.bounded_owner_retired: No separate test-only UPSERT model exists.

independent_review.notes: Broader conflict-target forms, internal trace equivalence, assurance, and independent review remain open.

known_blockers: Add composite, expression, partial, and multiple conflict-target support.
Generalize DO UPDATE assignment expressions and WHERE filtering.
Complete secondary-index conflict-cursor integration and independent fidelity review.

implementation_spans: Complete sqlite3UpsertAnalyzeTarget and sqlite3UpsertDoUpdate source bodies
Production bounded INSERT parser, action callback, foreign-key actions, and index maintenance
callees: B-tree table cursors and mutation APIs
assertions_branches_cleanup: Target uniqueness validation, IPK seek, collation-aware UNIQUE lookup, missed target, update, rollback, record cleanup, and hook publication reviewed
